name: Decline Cable Press
description: A cable chest press performed in a decline body position or with the cables set at a high angle to simulate a decline press vector. This arrangement maintains constant tension through the full pressing range of motion — unlike barbells or dumbbells that become lighter at lockout — while targeting the lower pectoralis major with a consistent force curve throughout the rep.

execution.starting_position: Set a decline bench inside a cable machine or face away from two high pulleys. On a decline bench: lie with head lower, cables running from behind and above. Hold handles at upper chest level, elbows bent.
execution.setup_instructions: Option 1: Use a cable machine with adjustable arms set to high position and lie on a decline bench below them. Option 2: Set a decline bench between two cable stacks with high pulleys. Attach single handles to each cable.
steps: Step 1: Lie on the decline bench, gripping cable handles at upper chest/shoulder level. Elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Step 2: Press the handles forward and downward (following the decline press vector) toward the lower chest area.
Step 3: Extend arms fully, feeling the constant cable tension even at lockout.
Step 4: Return under control to the starting position with elbows back at 90 degrees. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale to load the chest at the bottom, exhale during the press.
common_mistakes: Press direction going straight forward instead of slightly downward following the decline angle
Losing upper back contact with the bench during the press
Allowing cables to pull arms too far back behind the chest at the start
safety_considerations: Get a spotter or use a rack to position on the decline bench safely with cables attached
Secure feet firmly on the decline bench before initiating the press
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow extension at the top. At the bottom, elbows align with or slightly below the torso plane.
coaching_cues: Press along the decline line — think down and forward, not straight out
Feel the cables pulling at the top — that constant tension is the advantage over free weights
